AHT: Average handle time — the average duration of a customer interaction, including follow-up work.
API: Application programming interface — a defined way for software components to exchange data and commands.
APM: Application performance monitoring — measuring the performance and availability of applications and their dependencies.
CAB: Change Advisory Board — the group that assesses and advises on changes before they are authorized.
CI/CD: Continuous integration and continuous deployment — automated building, testing and release of software changes.
CIS: Center for Internet Security — publisher of widely used security configuration benchmarks.
CLI: Command-line interface — text-based administration of a device or system.
CMDB: Configuration management database — the record of configuration items and their relationships.
CRM: Customer relationship management — systems that manage an organization's interactions with its customers.
DeviceX: The SDX platform installed on standard Verto Wave hardware, delivered as a site appliance.
DevSecOps: The practice of building security into every stage of software development and operations.
DHCP: Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol — automatic assignment of IP addresses to devices.
DNS: Domain Name System — translation of names into network addresses.
DPI: Deep packet inspection — analysis of traffic content to identify applications and threats.
EDR: Endpoint detection and response — monitoring endpoints for threats and responding to them.
FCR: First-call resolution — the share of queries resolved in the first interaction.
GbE: Gigabit Ethernet — a network interface running at one gigabit per second.
IaC: Infrastructure as code — defining and provisioning infrastructure through version-controlled code.
IAX2: An open signaling and media transport protocol for voice over IP.
IDS: Intrusion detection system — detection of malicious activity in network traffic.
IoC: Indicator of compromise — evidence, such as an address or file hash, that a system may be compromised.
IoT: Internet of Things — connected sensors and devices.
IPS: Intrusion prevention system — detection and blocking of malicious activity in network traffic.
IPsec: Internet Protocol Security — a protocol suite that encrypts and authenticates IP traffic.
ITIL: A widely adopted framework of IT service management practices.
ITSM: IT service management — the processes and tools for delivering and supporting IT services.
IVR: Interactive voice response — an automated phone menu that routes or resolves calls.
KPI: Key performance indicator — a measure used to track performance against a goal.
LAN: Local area network — the network within a site.
LDAP: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol — a protocol for querying and managing directory information.
MFA: Multi-factor authentication — verifying identity with two or more independent factors.
MITRE ATT&CK: A public knowledge base of adversary tactics and techniques used to classify detections.
MOS: Mean opinion score — a measure of perceived voice quality on a scale of 1 to 5.
MPLS: Multiprotocol Label Switching — a carrier-provided private wide-area network service.
MTTD: Mean time to detect — the average time from the start of an incident to its detection.
MTTR: Mean time to resolve or respond — the average time to restore service or respond to an incident.
NAT: Network address translation — mapping of private addresses to public ones.
NDR: Network detection and response — analysis of network traffic to detect and respond to threats.
NVMe: Non-Volatile Memory Express — a high-speed interface for solid-state storage.
NVR: Network video recorder — a system that records and manages IP camera video.
OLA: Operations Level Agreement — the service levels agreed for the operations service.
ONVIF: An open industry standard for interoperability of IP-based security products such as cameras.
OSI: Open Systems Interconnection — the seven-layer reference model for network communication.
PCAP: Packet capture — a recorded copy of network traffic used for analysis and evidence.
PCI-DSS: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard — security requirements for handling card data.
PMI: Project Management Institute — the professional body whose standards define the project management process groups.
QoS: Quality of Service — prioritization of network traffic to meet performance needs.
RACI: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, Informed — a matrix that assigns roles for each activity.
RADIUS: Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service — a protocol for network access authentication.
RAID: Risks, actions, issues and decisions — the log used to control a project.
RBAC: Role-based access control — granting access through roles rather than to individuals.
REST: Representational State Transfer — a common style for web-based APIs.
SASE: Secure access service edge — combining networking and security services at the network edge.
SATA: Serial ATA — an interface for hard disks and solid-state drives.
SD-WAN: Software-defined wide-area network — an overlay that steers traffic across multiple access services.
SDX: The Verto Wave software platform that runs on DeviceX appliances.
SFP+: Enhanced small form-factor pluggable — a modular interface for 10 Gbps network links.
SIEM: Security information and event management — collection and correlation of security events.
SIP: Session Initiation Protocol — the signaling protocol for voice and video calls over IP.
SLA: Service level agreement — the service levels agreed between a provider and a customer.
SLI: Service level indicator — a measured value, such as latency or error rate, that indicates service health.
SLO: Service level objective — a target value for a service level indicator.
SNMP: Simple Network Management Protocol — a protocol for monitoring and managing network devices.
SOAR: Security orchestration, automation and response — automated execution of security playbooks.
SOC: Security operations center — the team and service that monitors and responds to security events.
SSH: Secure Shell — an encrypted protocol for remote administration.
StackX: The Verto Wave platform for observability, automation, service management and security operations.
STIX/TAXII: Open standards for describing and exchanging cyber threat intelligence.
TIP: Threat intelligence platform — a system that aggregates and applies threat intelligence.
TLS: Transport Layer Security — the protocol that encrypts traffic between applications.
UEBA: User and entity behavior analytics — detection of anomalous behavior by users, devices and accounts.
vCPU: Virtual CPU — a processor allocation for a virtual machine.
VLAN: Virtual local area network — a logical segment of a physical network.
VPN: Virtual private network — an encrypted connection across an untrusted network.
WAN: Wide-area network — the network connecting sites.
XDR: Extended detection and response — correlating endpoint, network and identity telemetry to detect threats.
